title: Review authoring and edit validation against pins
reason: merged locator#3, code-graph#13. Anchors are head/path#L10-L20, base/path#L7 or diff/path#L84-R90 with pins {repositoryId, head, base?} (packages/review/src/review-api/authoring-tools.ts:L43-L47); the edit path validates every new or changed source range and resource reference against the pins before saving (packages/review/src/review-api/store.ts:L1446-L1576), paths are checked lexically with no absolute, dot-dot or control characters (packages/review/src/source.ts:L40-L52), and the edit result quotes the first and last line of each anchor back to the agent. Titan HIL items cite code as free strings: evidenceRef up to 500 chars (gate-brief.ts), parts current/proposed as pasted code (titan-design schema), and codewatch questions only need to match path:line by regex (codewatch-questions.ts L46-L58). Adopt the anchor grammar and the accept-time range check (MIT) in owner-queue (an anchors field on OwnerItem and options) and round@2 parts, so a producer cannot file a Ship or A/B item that cites lines which do not exist at the pinned head. Feeds HIL-4b, HIL-11 and HIL-14; closes part of G11. Tests (wave 3) strengthen it: an anchor past the end of the pinned file, a reversed range, a path outside the repository and a whitespace-only range are each rejected at insert (packages/review/src/review-api/authoring-pitfalls.test.ts:L451-L475, L393); an edit whose source validation is suspended while another connection commits is rejected as stale (packages/review/src/review-api/authoring-session.test.ts:L123-L137); no part of an invalid edit and no failed repin is saved (packages/review/src/review-api/review-api.test.ts:L545, L1415); a repin keeps stale references and reports them for repair (review-api.test.ts:L449-L497). The accept-time check titan would port is tested at its boundary. Final merge: hitl-b#12 and locator#12 (source link and range validation tests) joined; worktree-base rows moved to LOC-06

title: Reader selection handed to agents
reason: merged locator#2. A reader selection is a strict schema: a text target with a block anchor holding block id, offsets and the text at selection time, or a code target with path, side and line range (packages/review/src/agent-selection.ts:L7-L44, L17-L29); the server turns it into a prompt that names the review id, version, pins and a quoted excerpt read at those pins (packages/review/src/review-api/http.ts:L1062-L1140). An owner answer in titan is optionId, free text and per-frame comments keyed by variant (owner-queue schema L32-L43); the harness pins are frame-key plus number (pins.ts). When the owner answers Request change, the implementer gets prose. Adopt the selection schema (MIT) as an optional anchors field on OwnerAnswer so HIL-3's listener can hand the woken implementer the exact lines at the exact head; it feeds HIL-3 and HIL-9b, and gap G11 for code options. Tests (wave 3): a selection serialises to Markdown with a range header and a diff fence, escapes code fences, uses pinned worktree roots and refuses graph selections (packages/review/src/agent-selection.test.ts:L5-L77); resolution rejects stale or reversed endpoints and needs base pins before touching the base side (packages/review/src/lens-selection.test.ts:L106-L123); diffr's viewer turns a selection into a git-style patch reference without inventing SHAs for a working tree (diffr/packages/viewer/src/document/selection.test.ts:L29-L83). Gap: the server's selectionContext prompt with the excerpt read at pins (http.ts:L1062-L1140) has no direct test, so a port takes the schema and resolution with their tests and needs its own excerpt test. Final merge: hitl-a#7 (diff selection to agent reference) joined
